subject: Kruschke (2015) style diagram for zero_inflated_beta model

messages.author: 689bc5eab59b4e7e
messages.subject: Kruschke (2015) style diagram for zero_inflated_beta model
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to visualize a brms model with zero_inflated_beta family using the conventions suggested by John Kruschke in his book Doing Bayesian Data Analysis. I used the LibreOffice template by Rasmus Bååth for a first sketch but I'm unsure if I'm correctly visualizing the zero-inflation and the beta part of the model. In case there's someone with more experience on how to visualize complex probabilistic models, I would highly appreciate some input or ideas on how to best display the zero_inflated_beta model in such a diagram. 

Here's some example code and the diagram:

# y_beta is beta distributed with some 0s
# x1, x2 are normaly distributed
# x2, x3, x4, x5, x6 are binary coded with 0/1
# model uses default priors (half student-t)
brm(bf(y_beta ~ x1+ x2 + x3, zi ~ x1 + x4 + x5 + x6), data, family = zero_inflated_beta)


Thanks!
